title: Tactics
description: Forks, pins, skewers, discovered and double checks, decoys, deflections, in-between moves, x-rays, overloaded and trapped pieces: the tricks that win material.

steps.text: A fork is a move that attacks two or more enemy pieces at once. Your opponent can only save one of them. Knights are famous for forks because they attack in so many directions.
Fork the king and rook, then collect the rook.
steps.success: A royal fork wins a whole rook.

steps.text: Pawns can fork too. Attack both black pieces at once.
steps.success: The pawn attacks the knight and the bishop, and it's protected: one of them will fall.

lessons.title: The pin
lessons.summary: Freeze a piece in front of a more valuable one.

steps.text: A pinned piece cannot move without exposing a more valuable piece behind it. When that piece is the king, moving the pinned piece is illegal — an absolute pin.
Pin the knight to the king. Your d-pawn will do the rest.
steps.hint: Line up your bishop with the knight and the king.
steps.success: The knight is pinned and can't move. Next d5 attacks it, and it's lost.

steps.text: Black's rook is pinned to its king by your bishop: it can't leave the diagonal. Attack it.
steps.success: The pinned rook can't run away. It will fall to the pawn.

steps.text: A skewer attacks a valuable piece that has a less valuable piece behind it. When the front piece moves out of the way, you capture the one behind.
Check the king along the e-file and win the queen behind it.
steps.hint: Your rook belongs on the e-file.

lessons.title: Discovered attacks
lessons.summary: Move one piece to unleash another.

steps.text: When a piece moves out of the way, it can uncover an attack by a piece behind it. If the uncovered attack is a check, the moving piece is free to grab almost anything.
Win the queen with a discovered check.
steps.hint: Move the bishop — the rook does the checking.
steps.success: Discovered check wins the queen for free.

lessons.title: Double check
lessons.summary: Two checks at once — only the king can answer.

steps.text: In a double check two pieces give check at the same time. Blocking or capturing can only deal with one of them, so the king has to move — and if it can't, it's checkmate. It happens when the piece that moves away gives check too.
Black's queen guards d8, but that won't matter. Mate in one.
steps.hint: Move the rook out of the bishop's way — with check.
steps.success: Double check and mate. The queen can't take the rook, because the bishop's check would remain.

lessons.title: Removing the defender
lessons.summary: Chase away the piece that holds everything together.

steps.text: White's queen and bishop are lined up at h7 (once White's own e4 pawn gets out of the way), and only the knight on f6 guards it. When one piece is doing all the defending, capture it, chase it away, or lure it off — and what it guarded falls.
Get rid of the defender of h7.
steps.hint: A pawn can attack the knight — and open the queen's diagonal at the same time.
steps.success: The knight had to leave f6, and h7 fell with mate.

steps.text: Black's queen has two jobs: guarding the rook on e8 and the knight on d4. A piece with two jobs is overloaded — force it to do one of them, and the other is left hanging.
Exploit the overloaded queen and win a piece.
steps.hint: Start with the capture that comes with check.
steps.success: The queen had to recapture on e8, and the knight on d4 was left without a defender.

steps.text: A piece with no safe squares is trapped: you can attack it at your leisure. Black's bishop grabbed the a2 pawn, and its only way back out is the a2–g8 diagonal.
Trap the bishop, then win it.
steps.hint: Block its diagonal with a pawn that's defended.
steps.success: The bishop is trapped — the best it can do is give itself up for a pawn.

lessons.title: The decoy
lessons.summary: Lure the king onto the wrong square.

steps.text: A decoy lures an enemy piece, often the king, onto a square where it can be attacked. From f7 White's knight would hit both d8 and h6. The queen is already on h6; now the king just has to be persuaded to come to d8.
Sacrifice to bring the king to d8, then fork king and queen with the knight.
steps.hint: Give up the rook with check on d8.
steps.success: The rook was bait: the king took it, and the knight fork won the queen.

lessons.title: Deflection
lessons.summary: Pull a defender away from its post.

steps.text: Deflection pulls a defender away from an important square. Black's rook on d8 guards the back rank: without it, Re8 would be mate, because Black's pawns box in the king. Find a capture the rook has to answer.
Deflect the rook from the back rank.
steps.hint: Offer a queen trade the rook would have to recapture.
steps.success: The rook took the bait and left the back rank. If Black doesn't recapture, White is simply a queen up.

lessons.title: Zwischenzug
lessons.summary: An in-between move before the expected recapture.

steps.text: A zwischenzug (German for 'in-between move') is a forcing move played before the move everyone expects. White's queen has just taken on d5. Taking back at once with ...Qxd5 only trades queens, because the knight on c3 guards d5. But nothing forces Black to recapture right away.
Win the queen with an in-between move.
steps.hint: Before taking back, remove the piece that guards d5, with check.
steps.success: Check first, recapture second: the guard is gone and Black wins the queen for a bishop.

steps.text: White's rook just took on d8. You'll take it back, but is there something better first?
steps.hint: Grab something with check, then take back on d8.
steps.success: Qxc1+ takes a rook with check, and Rxd8 then takes the other one: a whole rook up.

steps.text: Your rook on e8 can take back on e4. Look for an in-between capture first.
steps.success: The check bought the time to take both rooks.

lessons.title: X-ray
lessons.summary: A piece that works through another piece.

steps.text: An x-ray is a piece that attacks or defends through another piece. White's queen on a8 looks along the back rank through Black's queen on c8. So a rook on d8 would be defended twice over: once the black queen takes it, White's queen takes back.
Use the x-ray on the back rank.
steps.hint: Check on d8, even though the black queen covers it.
steps.success: Qxd8 was forced, and the queen behind it took back with mate.

steps.text: The queen on h5 looks through the bishop on f7 at e8. Make use of it.
steps.hint: Take the rook on e8 with check.
steps.success: When the bishop left f7 to take back, it opened the queen's x-ray: mate.

steps.text: Black's queen on h5 eyes d1 through White's queen on e2. Win the queen.
steps.hint: Check on d1: the white queen has to take, and then?
steps.success: The rook lured White's queen onto your queen's line: rook for queen.
